nodes.title: Questioning & Curiosity
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can ask a testable question about something they observe in the natural world.

nodes.title: Observation Skills
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can make and describe detailed qualitative observations using their senses and simple tools.

nodes.title: Scientific Method
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can list and order the steps of the scientific method and apply them to a simple guided investigation.

nodes.title: Basic Experimentation
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can carry out a simple hands-on experiment following given steps and report what happened.

nodes.title: Hypothesis Formation
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can state a testable, falsifiable hypothesis as an if-then prediction before an experiment.

nodes.title: Data Collection
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can gather measurements and observations during an investigation and record them systematically.

nodes.title: Measurement & Tools
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can choose and use appropriate tools and standard units to measure length, mass, volume, temperature, and time.

nodes.title: Data Recording
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can organize collected data into a labeled table or chart with correct units.

nodes.title: Variables & Controls
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify the independent, dependent, and controlled variables in an experiment.

nodes.title: Data Analysis (Basic)
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can read a data table or graph and describe the pattern or relationship it shows.

nodes.title: Scientific Models
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can build and use a diagram, physical, or conceptual model to represent a system or process.

nodes.title: Systems Thinking
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe a system in terms of its components, inputs, outputs, and interactions.

nodes.title: Scientific Communication
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can communicate findings clearly using scientific vocabulary, tables, and diagrams.

nodes.title: Lab Design
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can design a controlled investigation that tests a hypothesis with an appropriate procedure and controls.

nodes.title: Data Analysis (Advanced)
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can analyze data for trends, error, and uncertainty and judge whether it supports a claim.

nodes.title: Mathematical Modeling
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can use equations, rates, and proportional reasoning to model a scientific relationship quantitatively.

nodes.title: Theory & Explanation
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can construct an evidence-based explanation that connects observations to underlying scientific theory.

nodes.title: Independent Investigation
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can independently plan, conduct, and document an original scientific investigation end to end.

nodes.title: Scientific Mastery Project
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can produce and defend a complete research project with question, method, data, analysis, and conclusion.

nodes.title: Argument from Evidence
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can make a scientific claim and support or challenge it using relevant evidence and reasoning.

nodes.title: Properties of Matter
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe and sort objects by observable material properties such as color, texture, hardness, and flexibility.

nodes.title: States of Matter
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify solids, liquids, and gases and describe how heating and cooling change state.

nodes.title: Mixtures & Solutions
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can distinguish a mixture from a solution and describe how components can be separated.

nodes.title: Energy Types
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify forms of energy (kinetic, thermal, light, sound, electrical) and give examples of energy transfer.

nodes.title: Thermal Energy
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain heat transfer by conduction, convection, and radiation and predict temperature change.

nodes.title: Chemistry (Intro)
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe matter as made of particles and explain physical versus chemical properties.

nodes.title: Basic Chemistry
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can classify substances as elements, compounds, or mixtures and read a simple chemical formula.

nodes.title: Atoms and Molecules
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe the structure of an atom (protons, neutrons, electrons) and how atoms combine into molecules.

nodes.title: Periodic Table
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can use the periodic table to find an element's symbol, atomic number, and group and period.

nodes.title: Chemistry Reactions
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can interpret a balanced chemical equation and identify reactants and products.

nodes.title: Chemical Reactions
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify evidence of a chemical reaction and describe how new substances are formed.

nodes.title: Conservation of Matter
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain that matter is conserved in physical and chemical changes and mass does not disappear.

nodes.title: Chemical Bonding
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can distinguish ionic from covalent bonds and explain why atoms bond.

nodes.title: Advanced Chemistry
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can apply stoichiometry, bonding, and reaction types to solve multi-step chemistry problems.

nodes.title: Physics (Intro)
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe motion using position, speed, and direction and represent it on a graph.

nodes.title: Forces and Motion
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify forces acting on an object and predict how balanced and unbalanced forces change its motion.

nodes.title: Newton's Laws of Motion
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can state and apply Newton's three laws of motion to explain everyday phenomena.

nodes.title: Gravity
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain gravity as an attractive force between masses and describe its effect on falling objects and orbits.

nodes.title: Simple Machines
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify the six simple machines and explain how each changes force or motion to do work.

nodes.title: Magnetism
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe magnetic poles, attraction and repulsion, and identify magnetic materials.

nodes.title: Electricity & Circuits
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can build a simple circuit and explain the roles of a source, conductor, switch, and load.

nodes.title: Waves
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe a wave by its amplitude, wavelength, and frequency and how it transfers energy.

nodes.title: Light
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain how light travels, reflects, and refracts and how we see objects and colors.

nodes.title: Sound
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain that sound is produced by vibrations and relate pitch and volume to frequency and amplitude.

nodes.title: Physics Systems
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can analyze energy transfer and conservation within a physical system.

nodes.title: Advanced Physics
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can apply quantitative laws of motion, energy, and forces to solve multi-step physics problems.

nodes.title: Biology (Intro)
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can distinguish living from non-living things and describe the basic needs of organisms.

nodes.title: Animal Biology
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe basic animal needs, life cycles, and how animals are grouped by shared features.

nodes.title: Plant Biology
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can name the parts of a plant and describe what plants need to grow and reproduce.

nodes.title: Cells
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify a cell as the basic unit of life and label major parts of plant and animal cells.

nodes.title: Photosynthesis & Respiration
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain how plants make food by photosynthesis and how cells release energy through respiration.

nodes.title: Ecosystems
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe how organisms in an ecosystem interact and depend on their environment.

nodes.title: Food Webs
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can trace the flow of energy through a food chain and food web from producers to consumers to decomposers.

nodes.title: Human Body
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can name major external and internal body parts and describe their basic functions.

nodes.title: Body Systems
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe the major human body systems and how they work together to keep the body alive.

nodes.title: Microorganisms
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe bacteria, viruses, and fungi and explain their helpful and harmful roles.

nodes.title: Biology Systems
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain how structures and processes in an organism function as interacting systems.

nodes.title: Heredity & Genetics
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can use dominant and recessive traits and a Punnett square to predict inheritance.

nodes.title: DNA
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe DNA as the molecule that stores genetic information and how genes code for traits.

nodes.title: Evolution & Natural Selection
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain how natural selection acts on variation to drive evolution over generations.

nodes.title: Advanced Biology
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can analyze complex biological processes and connect molecular, cellular, and ecosystem levels.

nodes.title: Earth Science
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe Earth's major materials and features and the basic land, water, and air systems.

nodes.title: Rock Cycle
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can classify rocks as igneous, sedimentary, or metamorphic and describe how the rock cycle transforms them.

nodes.title: Plate Tectonics
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain how moving plates cause earthquakes, volcanoes, and mountain formation.

nodes.title: Weather Patterns
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can read weather instruments and describe how temperature, air pressure, and moisture create weather.

nodes.title: Water Cycle
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and collection in the water cycle.

nodes.title: Earth's Systems
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe how the geosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere, and biosphere interact.

nodes.title: Natural Resources
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can distinguish renewable from non-renewable resources and explain conservation of Earth's resources.

nodes.title: Earth History
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can use rock layers and fossils to describe the relative age and history of Earth.

nodes.title: Solar System
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can name the planets in order and describe the Sun, Moon, and their motions in the solar system.

nodes.title: Moon Phases & Seasons
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain the cause of moon phases and of seasons using Earth's tilt and orbit.

nodes.title: Space Science
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe stars, galaxies, and gravity's role in the structure and motion of the universe.

nodes.title: Galaxies & Universe
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe galaxies and the scale and expansion of the universe supported by evidence.

nodes.title: Climate & Environment
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe how living things and human activity interact with and affect the environment.

nodes.title: Climate Change
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain the greenhouse effect and cite evidence for human-caused climate change and its impacts.

nodes.title: Weather vs Climate
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can distinguish day-to-day weather from long-term climate using data over time.

nodes.title: Engineering Design Process
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can follow the engineering design cycle to define, plan, build, test, and improve a solution.

nodes.title: Defining Problems
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can define a simple design problem including its criteria for success and constraints.

nodes.title: Testing Solutions
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can build and fairly test a prototype, compare it to criteria, and use results to improve it.

merges.note: Overlap SP: SC-EX001 Scientific Method overlaps the granular practices spine SC2 Questioning -> SC3 Basic Experimentation -> ... SC-EX001 RETAINED as the umbrella intro (distinct game skill) and wired as a Fluency node above SC2/SC3 (hard SC-EX002; soft SC2, SC3). The step-by-step practices (SC2-SC17) remain the canonical practices spine. No node removed. SC-EX001 keeps its cross_domain edges to Math (M-029/M-062/M-063).

Overlap Chemistry-1: SC-EX005 Basic Chemistry duplicates SC21 Chemistry (Intro). SC21 is the canonical Chemistry branch entry (gated on SC8 Data Analysis); SC-EX005 RETAINED as its concrete first atomic (hard SC21). Both are distinct game skills.

Overlap Chemistry-2: SC-EX007 Chemical Reactions duplicates SC22 Chemistry Reactions. SC22 canonical spine node; SC-EX007 RETAINED as the concrete reactions atomic (hard SC-EX005, soft SC-EX008). Both retained as distinct game skills.

Overlap Chemistry-3: SC-EX008 Atoms and Molecules is the atomic-structure content feeding toward SC23 Advanced Chemistry (via SC-305 Periodic Table, SC-307 Chemical Bonding). SC-EX008 RETAINED as an Application atomic; SC23 stays the Mastery capstone.

Overlap Physics-1: SC-EX009 Forces and Motion duplicates SC24 Physics (Intro). SC24 canonical branch entry (gated on SC8); SC-EX009 RETAINED as its concrete first atomic (hard SC24). Stage corrected Integration -> Application.

Overlap Physics-2: SC-EX010 Energy Types overlaps SC25 Physics Systems (energy transfer/conservation). SC-EX010 RETAINED as the elementary energy atomic (Physical Science cluster, hard SC-EX002) that soft-feeds SC25. Stage corrected Integration -> Fluency.

Overlap Physics-3: SC-EX011 Simple Machines and SC-EX012 Magnetism are concrete physics atomics under the Physics discipline (SC24 -> SC25 -> SC26). Both RETAINED; stages corrected Integration -> Fluency (these are elementary topics).

Overlap Biology-1: SC-EX013 Plant Biology and SC-EX014 Animal Biology are the concrete intro-biology atomics under SC18 Biology (Intro). SC18 canonical branch entry; SC-EX013/014 RETAINED. Removed the odd Plant->Animal hard edge; made them siblings under SC18.

Overlap Biology-2: SC-EX015 Ecosystems and SC-EX016 Human Body are concrete life-science content that feeds SC19 Biology Systems. Both RETAINED as atomics; SC19 stays the systems-level branch node. Ecosystems stage corrected Foundations -> Fluency.

Overlap Earth-1: SC-EX017 Weather Patterns and SC-EX018 Rock Cycle are the concrete Earth-science atomics under SC27 Earth Science. SC27 canonical branch entry; both RETAINED. Stages corrected Mastery -> Fluency.

Overlap Earth-2: SC-EX020 Climate Change duplicates the environmental strand of SC28 Climate & Environment. SC28 canonical Environmental-Science branch; SC-EX020 RETAINED as its concrete atomic (hard SC28). Stage corrected Mastery -> Application.

Overlap Space-1: SC-EX019 Solar System is the concrete intro-astronomy atomic feeding SC29 Space Science. SC29 stays the integration-level branch (hard SC-EX019); SC-EX019 RETAINED. Detached the spurious Rock Cycle->Solar System hard edge. Stage corrected Mastery -> Fluency.
